title: Pollination and Seed Dispersal
seo_title: Grade 2 Pollination and Seed Dispersal Worksheets: How Animals Help Plants
standard_text: Develop a simple model that mimics the function of an animal in dispersing seeds or pollinating plants.
meta_desc: Free grade 2 science worksheets on pollination and seed dispersal (NGSS 2-LS2-2): how bees move pollen, how seeds travel, and simple models. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_sub: Bees move pollen. Animals, wind and water move seeds.
body_html:
How to think about it

Animals help plants make and spread seeds.

  • Pollination: bees and birds move pollen.
  • Seed dispersal: fur, eating, burying, wind, water.
  • A model shows how it works.
Example

A bee drinks nectar and gets pollen on its body. Then it visits another flower. What happens?

It moves pollen.

Answer: pollination

Example

A burr sticks to a dog's fur and falls off far away. What happens?

The seed moves.

Answer: seed dispersal

Common mistakes

  • Thinking bees make flowers grow taller. They move pollen.
  • Thinking pollen is food for the plant.
  • Mixing up pollination (pollen) and seed dispersal (seeds).

faq.a: Moving pollen from flower to flower so the plant can make seeds. Bees, butterflies and hummingbirds do this.
On animal fur, inside animals that eat fruit, buried by squirrels, blown by wind or floating on water.
A cotton ball or pipe cleaner bee that picks up chalk pollen, or a fuzzy sock that picks up seeds.
